text:
maya: Heads-up — saw a cluster of tenants still routing to v1 after the deprec rollout yesterday. Console shows them as 'upgraded', but request telemetry contains X-Client-Version: v1 and the handshake TTL looks expired.

maya: Log sample:
```
tenant=acme-corp req_id=01FZ7Q header="X-Client-Version: v1" route_requested=/v2/generate routed_to=v1 latency=22ms
``` 

chris: How many tenants and what's the quota impact?

maya: ~18 tenants, spike ~3k req/min to v1 for ~10m which pushed a couple of Dedicated tenants over soft-quota -> 429s. Not all appear to be on old SDKs (some recent clients).

sasha: Possible vectors: console pin override, token->route affinity, or client-side header caching. We saw header coalescing before in the proxy. :thinking: 

alex: Another suspect is our handshake TTL logic. If handshake_ts isn't refreshed after a failed canary attempt, we keep honoring the last client header indefinitely. We currently prefer client header when present.

alex: Pseudocode of current behavior:
```
if client_header_present:
  route = client_header_version
elif now - handshake_ts < TTL:
  route = cached_handshake_version
else:
  route = default_server_version
```

alex: Suggestion: when handshake TTL expired, ignore client header for a single canary attempt to v2, then fall back if it fails. Also emit a telemetry counter for "handshake_mismatch_count" and per-tenant "stuck_version" flag.

maya: If we can surface a per-tenant "routing health" card in Console (shows last handshake, last header, and a "force re-handshake" action) that'd make ops triage much faster.

chris: Force re-handshake exists as an internal endpoint (`POST /internal/tenant/{id}/routing/refresh`), but it's risky: clears cache immediately and can cause mass re-roll to new model. Need audit + rate-limit + UI confirmation.

sasha: For immediate mitigation, we could run a dry-run: count requests that would have gone to v2 if we ignored the header when TTL expired. Add a sampling debug flag so we can measure impact without changing routing.

maya: I like the dry-run first. Metrics team: can we add a sampled gauge `would_switch_to_v2` tagged by tenant and reason? Even a 1% sample across tenants would help.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: `routing/ttl-fallback-dryrun` -> 10% tenants. :rocket:

chris: Also double-check quota accounting: billing must follow the final routed variant, not the header. If we calc quota off header we could under-account or double-count.

sasha: I'll open a small PR: (1) add `would_switch_to_v2` sampling metric, (2) change TTL fallback to attempt single canary to v2 on expiry (dry-run mode first), (3) add an alert if >5% of active tenants would switch.

alex: Good. After data looks clean, we can wire Console: routing health + a controlled "force re-handshake" with audit trail.

maya: Thanks — please spam the PR link here when ready and let's coordinate an ops window if we flip behavior. If any tenant experiences customer-facing errors we'll run the rollback playbook and write a postmortem.

chris: Noted. Putting a small Runbook note in the channel for the weekend ops on-call.

sasha: PR coming in ~30m. Will include unit tests for header-ignore logic and a small load-test snippet to simulate fallback.

maya: Perfect.
